evidence.detail: archetype.keyCards.shift() mutates the keyCards array in-place during render, removing the first element from the object stored in React state
archetype.keyCards[0] is used earlier in the same render for the main hero card image; after .shift() runs, subsequent renders see a different [0] element, causing the visible image to change
componentDidUpdate calls load() on sort change without clearing objects; old (now mutated) objects are rendered while the network request is in flight, producing the flash

triage.fix_sketch: In shared_web/static/js/metagamegrid.jsx line 81, replace `archetype.keyCards.shift()` with a non-mutating check: `archetype.keyCards.length > 1` as the guard, and `archetype.keyCards.slice(1).map(...)` to render the remaining cards. This prevents mutation of the state object and eliminates the inter-render drift in keyCards[0].
triage.notes: One-line fix. The mutation bug means every sort/reload re-render shows progressively shorter key-card arrays as .shift() has already consumed elements. The fix also incidentally corrects this accumulating data-loss on repeated renders.
